According to the Chinese press, 10,000 Japanese
troops are reported to have landed at Mirs Bay, 16
miles north-east of Hongkong and 14 miles south-west
of Bias Bay at dawn on December 20. These troops
are said to be advancing towards Waiyeung and Chwanmutow,
a railway station of the Canton-Kowloon Line.
----
In our report of December 20 we indicated that two
representatives of the Shanghai 'Ta Tao' Municipal
Government were to proceed at 9.45 a.m. that morning to
the Shanghai Municipal Bank, 462 Avenue Joffre in order
to take over control. Mr. CHOW HWAN TSANG, manager,
who received Messrs. LOU YU JU (residing at Passage 160,
423 Ave. Foch, French Concession) and TSUNG CHUNG MEI,
the representatives in question, refused and stated
that the management of the Bank would meet in order
to discuss the matter. LOU and TSUNG then withdrew
after handing to Mr. CHOW a letter, the translation
of which follows:

November 20.
To the Shanghai Municipal Bank.

I have the honour to bring to your notice
that I have received Order No. 1, Character "Fu"
of the Shanghai Ta Tao Municipal Government, con-
ceived in the following terms:

"Our personal secretary Mr. CHING CHIEN
is designated by the present order to occupy
himself with the duties of assistant manager of
the Shanghai Municipal Bank. He is requested
to proceed to the bank immediately and to take
over his duties and to report to us thereon."

I am sending you Messrs. LOU YU JU and TSUNG
CHUNG MEI with the request that they be shown the
balance sheet (debits and credits), seals, amounts
deposited, etc., etc., and that they be handed
over to them. I will make an official visit in
a few days in order to take over control of the
Bank.

(Signed and sealed) CHING CHIEN.

11月20日。
致上海市政银行。

Eight Japanese transports arrived in Shanghai on
December 15. Four of them landed about 1000 troops,

towards Nanchang, whilst the other three took

The new lines of defence of the Chinese troops are:
between Luno (NE of Nanking), Chuchow (NW of Pukow),

and seven of the 14 machines which took to the air to

reported to have observed more than forty bombing
planes on the ground, the majority of which were
Martin machines.

REPORT DATED DECEMBER 20, 1937
D. 8039 A
21 / 12 / 37

The 'Social Daily News' announces that important
modifications are about to be brought into the organisation
of the Chinese High Command. The operations in Shansi, it
is said, will be directed by the commander of the Eighth
Route Army (ex-communist). CHU TEH is reported to have been
appointed Commander-in-chief. He will probably be assisted
by PENG TEH HUAI and HSU HSIANG CHUAN. General LI TSUNG JEN.
C-in-C of troops operating in the Tsingpu sector, will be
recalled to Hankow in order that he may direct military
operations on the Pingnan front. He will be replaced by
Gen. TANG SHEN CHIH, ex-commander of the Nanking Defence
activities.

Troops concentrated in Anhwei and Kiangsi will be
placed under the direct orders of Gen. PAI KUNG HSI.

Gen. CHANG FAH KWEI will continue to command the troops
on the Hangchow front.

（印：NCH 21 DEC 1937）
A new army has been formed in Hangchow for the defence
of Chekiang. It has been placed under the orders of Gen.
HUANG SHAO HSIUNG, President of the Chekiang
Provincial Government. His Chief of Staff is Gen. LI WEI
WEN. The army comprises six independent brigades - 1st.,
6th., 34th., 35th., 38th., and 45th.

On the Hangchow sector the Japanese are reported to be

TRANSLATION OF FRENCH POLICE REPORT NO.2051/B DATED 20.9.37.
SUBJECT: Mme. Chiang Kai Shek's visit to Shanghai.

Madame CHIANG KAI SHEK, accompanied by two armed body- 8039A/M
guards and a personal maid, arrived here at 2.11.20 a.m. Septem- 21 9 37
ber 18, by the Shanghai Nanking highway via Soochow.

She entered the Settlement by Brenan Road. As her body
guards were armed, the British soldiers on duty prevented Mme.
CHIANG and her suite from entering the Settlement. After
a certain amount of argument, a British officer permitted Mme.
CHIANG to telephone to her brother, Dr. T.V. SOONG, who arrived
on the spot a short time later. Thanks to the efforts of Dr.
SOONG, Mme. CHIANG was able to proceed. She went direct to
the residence of Dr. H.H. KUNG, where she arrived at 1.35 p.m.
She had an interview there with Madame KUNG. At about 4 p.m.
she proceeded to her own home at 9 Route Francis Garnier. At
5.10 p.m. she left and returned to the KUNG residence. At
7 p.m. Mme. CHIANG KAI SHEK, accompanied by her brother, left
by car for Soochow via Route Ghisi. At Soochow Dr. T.V. SOONG
had an interview of an important nature with the Generalissimo.
Dr. SOONG returned to Shanghai at 5 a.m. on the 19th. After
his arrival he made his way to 262 Route Fergusson, the home of
Mr. MAZOT, and remained there until 11 a.m. when he went to his
own residence.

As a result of the trouble which Mme. CHIANG KAI SHEK
had with the British Military Post at Brenan Road, the Chinese
Authorities are reported to have decided to advise Chinese
notables going to or from Shanghai to make use of the Route
Ghisi entrance into the French Concession or Settlement.

--------

Extract from the daily bulletin of the S.M.P. dated 18.9.1937.
Madame Chiang Kai Shek arrived in Shanghai from Nanking
at 11 a.m. September 18 by road. Madame Chiang's car was
escorted by two other cars containing bodyguards. She
is at present residing at 531 Rue Hervé (la Bièvre), the
residence of Mr. T.V. Soong.

1937年9月20日法国警察报告第2051/B号译文。
主题：蒋介石夫人访问上海。

蒋介石夫人由两名武装保镖和一名贴身女仆陪同，于9月18日凌晨2点11分20秒经苏州通过上海-南京公路抵达此处。

她经由布伦南路（Brenan Road）进入租界。由于她的保镖携带武器，执勤的英国士兵阻止蒋夫人及其随行人员进入租界。经过一番争论，一名英国军官允许蒋夫人给她的哥哥宋子文博士打电话，宋博士不久后赶到现场。得益于宋博士的努力，蒋夫人得以通行。她直接前往孔祥熙博士的住所，于下午1点35分到达。她在那里与孔夫人进行了会谈。下午4点左右，她前往自己位于高乃伊路（Route Francis Garnier）9号的家中。下午5点10分离开，返回孔宅。晚上7点，蒋介石夫人在哥哥的陪同下，乘车经吉希路（Route Ghisi）前往苏州。在苏州，宋子文博士与委员长进行了一次重要会谈。宋博士于19日凌晨5点返回上海。抵达后，他前往马佐（MAZOT）先生位于费格斯逊路262号的家中，并在那里停留至上午11点，随后回到自己的住所。

据报道，由于蒋夫人在布伦南路英国军事哨所遇到的麻烦，中国当局决定建议往返上海的中国名人使用法租界或公共租界的吉希路入口。

--------

摘自1937年9月18日工部局警务处每日简报。
蒋夫人于9月18日上午11点由陆路从南京抵达上海。蒋夫人的汽车由两辆载有保镖的汽车护送。她目前居住在赫维路（Rue Hervé，即拉比耶夫路 la Bièvre）531号，即宋子文先生的住所。

（批：B.C. C.S.D.）

"Hwa Liei Wan Pao" du 15 septembre, rapporte que les unités
de la 8ème armée de marche (anciennes troupes rouges) sont
arrivées le 13 à Yuanping (à 125 km. environ au nord de
Taiyuan - Shansi), en route pour Tatung.

第二部分
C. 关于中国红军的情报。
第八路军据说将被调往山西。
9月15日的《华列晚报》（Hwa Liei Wan Pao）转载了一封来自北京的私人电报，称第八路军（原红军部队）的单位已于13日抵达原平（位于山西北部，距太原约125公里），正在前往大同途中。

5.45 p.m. August 22 from the French Police:

The transport "Shiretoko" capable of carrying 2,000
men arrived at 4 p.m. August 22, and is lying at the China
Merchants Central Wharf. Marines are now being landed.

Four Japanese cruisers are taking up positions viz.
Natori - Buoys 9-10 } Midstream.
Yubary - " 13-14 }

Two other cruisers are lying in midstream facing
the "China Transport Wharf" in such a position as to suggest
that an attempt will be made to land troops at Tungkou,
Pootung.

9.50 p.m. August 22

The French Police report that there is a French
citizen residing at either 161 Thomas Road or in 81 Park Lane (43)
Thorburn Road and wished to know whether it will be possible
to locate her. Her name is Madame Villiard. (Hongkew
communicated with: both these addresses are on the other side
of the Hongkew Creek and nothing can be done at the moment.)

10.25 p.m. August 22:

Listening in to "Evening Post" broadcast as per
instructions. The words "convicts were pushed through
the British lines in the Western District at 1 p.m. to-day"
were used but the whole tone of the broadcast was completely
innocuous.

下午5时45分，8月22日，来自法国警察局的报告：

可容纳2,000人的运输船“知床丸”（Shiretoko）于8月22日下午4时抵达，现停泊在招商局中央码头。海军陆战队正在登陆。

四艘日本巡洋舰正在占据阵位，即：
名取号（Natori）——9-10号浮标 } 江心。
夕张号（Yubary）——13-14号浮标 }

另有两艘巡洋舰停泊在江心，正对“中国运输码头”，其阵位表明日军可能试图在浦东东沟（Tungkou）登陆部队。

晚上9时50分，8月22日

法国警察局报告称，有一位法国公民居住在托马斯路（Thomas Road）161号或派克巷（Park Lane）81号（索本路（Thorburn Road）43号），希望了解是否能找到她。她的名字是维利亚尔夫人（Madame Villiard）。（已与虹口方面联络：这两个地址均在虹口港对岸，目前无法采取行动。）

晚上10时25分，8月22日：

按照指示收听《晚邮报》（Evening Post）的广播。广播中使用了“今日下午1时，囚犯被推过西区英军防线”的字眼，但整个广播的语气完全无害。

TRANSLATION FROM FRENCH POLICE MILITARY BULLETIN
OF AUGUST 22,1937
------------------

Following an arrangement made between the Shanghai
Municipal Council and the Chinese Judicial Authorities,
5,900 of the 6,231 prisoners at present in Ward Road
Gaol, will be freed in lots of 500 as from midday to-day.
The first 500 was evacuated by the Settlement Police
without difficulty and escorted to the limit of the
British Defence Sector at the spot where the railway
crosses Great Western Road.

The rumour reproduced in the American newspaper
"Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury" that these prisoners
were going to be incorporated in the Chinese Army was
immediately followed by Japanese reaction, opposition
being shown to the departure of the second batch of
prisoners which should have taken place at 4 p.m.

-----

Jiu

1937年8月22日法国警察局军事公报译文
------------------

根据上海工部局与中国司法当局达成的安排，目前在提篮桥监狱（Ward Road Gaol）的6,231名囚犯中的5,900人，将从今日中午起以每批500人的规模释放。首批500人由租界警察顺利撤出，并护送至英军防御区边界，地点位于铁路与大西路（Great Western Road）交叉处。

美国报纸《上海晚邮报与水星报》（Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury）刊登谣言称，这些囚犯将被编入中国军队，此举立即引发日方反应，日方对原定于下午4时出发的第二批囚犯的离开表示反对。

-----

Jiu
